newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar to set up fifth petrochemical project.
newsitem.headline: Qatar to set up fifth petrochemical project.

text.p: Oil and gas-rich Qatar is planning to set up a petrochemical project in partnership with three U.S. companies, Qatari officials said on Saturday.
"Negotiations...to set up an ethylene cracker project are at an advanced stage and we hope to sign a deal soon," Qatar's Minister of Energy and Industry Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah told reporters.

The three companies involved are Phillips Petroleum Co, Dow Chemical Co and Nova Corp, said Attiyah, who did not disclose the production capacity or the cost of the project, the fifth such one to be negotiated by Qatar. But officials at the state's Qatar General Petroleum Corporation (QGPC) told Reuters the cost would be around $500 million.

They said QGPC will hold 50 percent and the remainder will be shared among the three foreign partners. As with all Qatari projects, 70 percent of the cost will be raised by buyers' credit and commercial loans and 30 percent will be contributed by shareholders.

The ethylene cracker project is the fifth petrochemical unit in a series of several multibillion-dollar gas and gas-based schemes designed and being executed by the Gulf Arab state to tap its enormous North Field gas reserves -- the largest in the world.
